about: What sixty-seven annual town reports say about Lunenburg, 1959 to FY2025: the tax rate, the population, the longest names on the school rosters and the road to a town manager.

conclusions.basis: The tax rate on each edition’s fact page, and the three revaluation passages quoted below.
conclusions.claim: The tax rate peaked at $133.00 per $1,000 in the 1969 report; FY2025 prints $14.36
conclusions.detail: The plotted series falls by more than a third from one edition to the next 3 times, and each fall sits beside a report saying the town revalued property that year. A lower rate on higher values is not a lower tax bill.
conclusions.not_shown: What a household paid in any year. The reports print a rate and a town valuation, not a typical bill, before 1976.
conclusions.so_what: A rate only compares within one assessment, and the reports record three revaluations.

conclusions.basis: `staff-roster-entries.csv`, names matched with middle initials and titles dropped.
conclusions.claim: The name Richard A. Stachowicz is printed on school rosters from 1963 to 2001
conclusions.detail: 38 years, printed in 34 of the 35 roster editions we hold for them. A span is first to last appearance, not a hire or a retirement date.
conclusions.not_shown: Years outside the reports we hold, and whether a gap year was leave or a roster that left the name out.
conclusions.so_what: The longest unbroken run of any name across every school roster we hold.

conclusions.basis: The reports quoted in the timeline, and the printed election return.
conclusions.claim: A study first recommended a town manager in 1966; the charter came in 1999
conclusions.detail: 33 years. The charter question passed 422 to 150 at the annual town election; two study committees came before it.
conclusions.not_shown: Why it took that long. The reports record the steps, not the arguments at the meetings in between.
conclusions.so_what: The post began as the CAFO; the 2009 report is the first with a Town Manager section.

conclusions.basis: The population line on each edition’s fact page.
conclusions.claim: Population went from 5,282 in 1955 to 10,280 in 2010
conclusions.detail: Each figure is the one a report’s fact page prints, by the year it counts rather than the edition that reprinted it.
conclusions.not_shown: Anything after the last census a fact page prints; the FY reports stopped printing a population.
conclusions.so_what: Nearly twice the people on the same land: both fact pages print 26.63 square miles.

conclusions.basis: The 1968 report’s five-year table (it reprints 1950) and the 2010 report’s valuation history.
conclusions.claim: The town raised $251,843 by taxation in 1950 and levied $17,427,297 in FY2010
conclusions.detail: That is 69 times the 1950 figure, before any allowance for prices, population or what the town now does.
conclusions.not_shown: The real change. Nothing here deflates a 1950 dollar.
conclusions.so_what: Nominal dollars: the only price index held here starts in 1990, so none is applied.

conclusions.claim: The first aide on the rosters is in 1970; the 2025 roster prints 52
conclusions.detail: Dorothy Hillman, “Teacher Aide for Perceptually Handicapped Program”. Counted from roster entries classified as paraprofessional.
conclusions.not_shown: Hours or funding. A roster line is a name, not a full-time post, and some years print names with no role to classify.
conclusions.so_what: A job the earliest rosters never print is now the second most printed, after classroom teachers.

conclusions.basis: The Assessors’ 1910-1960 comparison table. “Camp” is not defined there; the gloss is local knowledge (TJ, 30 October 2026).
conclusions.claim: In 1960 the Assessors counted 452 camps beside 1,734 dwelling houses
conclusions.detail: 21% of the 2,186 homes the table counts. The 1960 report is the only edition we hold that prints a camp count.
conclusions.not_shown: Where the camps were, or when they became year-round homes: no later report prints the category.
conclusions.so_what: A camp is a seasonal house, not lived in year-round; 1910 printed none.

conclusions.basis: `staff-roster-entries.csv`, the entries quoted in the roster section.
conclusions.claim: Genevieve Nass: a school cook from 1961 to 1981, then a name under Phys. Ed. from 1999
conclusions.detail: Matched on the name alone this would be the longest run on the rosters, 42 years. A run here breaks on a long absence for exactly this reason.
conclusions.not_shown: Whether the two careers are one person. Same name is not same person.
conclusions.so_what: Absent from 14 rosters in between; whether it is one person, no report says.

conclusions.basis: The 1959 report: the election return, the special election, and the Selectmen’s own report.
conclusions.claim: In 1959 the race for Selectman tied, 853 votes to 853
conclusions.detail: The count the report prints as the original, before the recount. Howard A. Hamel won the May special election over Eino O. Toko.
conclusions.not_shown: What the recount found. The report prints the original count and the special election, not the recount’s figures.
conclusions.so_what: A special election in May decided it, 1,238 to 1,216; the board was a member short until then.

conclusions.basis: The 1959 report, Town Clerk; its last column agrees with the clerk’s list of services on the next page.
conclusions.claim: The Town Clerk recorded 90 births in 1950 and 138 in 1956
conclusions.detail: From a 10-year chart of births, marriages and deaths the clerk printed in the last report of the decade: births the office recorded.
conclusions.not_shown: Why births rose. The chart is a count; it gives no cause.
conclusions.so_what: No later year in the clerk’s chart fell back to the 1950 figure.

grain: MIXED, AND EACH FIGURE SAYS WHICH. A tax rate is dollars per $1,000 of assessed value, as printed; a population is residents in the year the figure counts; a roster run is years between first and last appearance of a name. Dollars are nominal.
not_established: Whether a name on two rosters is one person. The rosters print names, not employee numbers.
Hire and retirement dates. A run is first and last appearance in the reports we hold.
Any comparison in real dollars. The price index held here starts in 1990.
What a household paid in tax in any year before the reports printed an average bill.
Staffing levels. A roster line is a name, with no hours and no funding source.
The years the archive has no report for, and the pages our reading did not yield.

town_manager.what: A study committee names a town manager as its preferred form.

town_manager.label: 1983 Annual Town Report
town_manager.quote: investigate the establishment of a Selectmen-Town Manager form of government
town_manager.what: A second study committee is appointed for the same question.

town_manager.quote: Adoption of the new charter resulted in an increased membership in the Board of Selectmen, the Board of Health and the creation of a new position, Chief Administrative Financial Officer (CAFO)
town_manager.what: A Home Rule Charter creates the post, under another name: CAFO.

town_manager.quote: resulted in the hiring of William J. Gustus to fill the position
